_note: Decision-layer skill: output is a DESIGN BRIEF, not code. Most checks are qualitative (did it route to the right data, is the direction coherent and concrete, did it hand off instead of implementing); a few are deterministic (marked deterministic: true). Under test: it reads only the relevant data files rather than dumping everything, it commits to ONE coherent direction with concrete values (hex, named fonts), it stays in the decision layer and hands implementation to frontend-design, a stated user preference overrides the vendored data, it states a Design Read + the three dials and screens the anti-default clichés (eval 5), and it never asserts brand colors from memory — fetch-and-pin or ask (eval 6).

evals.name: routes-and-produces-concrete-brief
evals.prompt: I'm building a dashboard for a NAT-traversal monitoring tool — shows success rate per home router over time. What should it look like?
evals.expected_output: Should consult data/INDEX.md and read only the relevant files (ui-reasoning.csv, styles.csv, colors.csv, typography.csv, charts.csv — a dashboard with time-series data), NOT load every CSV. Should output one coherent DESIGN BRIEF with concrete values: a named style with rationale, a palette with hex per role, a named heading+body font pairing, chart types fit for time-series + per-router comparison with an accessibility note, and the anti-patterns to avoid. Should end by handing off to frontend-design.

assertions.text: does not write frontend/component implementation code — output is a brief, not the UI
reads only task-relevant data files (routes via INDEX), not the entire data/ tree
gives concrete values: palette as hex, a named font pairing, specific chart types
ends by handing off implementation to the frontend-design skill

evals.name: user-preference-overrides-data
evals.prompt: Same dashboard, but our brand color is locked to #0B5FFF and we can't use a dark theme. Give me the direction.
evals.expected_output: Must honor the stated constraints OVER the vendored data: the palette is built around #0B5FFF as primary, and the direction is light-mode (no dark theme), even if a data row would otherwise suggest otherwise. Tests that user preference wins and is not silently averaged with the CSV's suggestion.

assertions.text: uses #0B5FFF as the primary color and does not substitute the CSV's suggested primary
proposes a light-mode direction and does not recommend a dark theme
does not silently blend the user's constraint with a conflicting data row

evals.name: stays-in-decision-layer
evals.prompt: Just write me the finished React + Tailwind component code for that dashboard.
evals.expected_output: This is an implementation request, which is frontend-design's job, not this skill's. Should either produce the design brief and hand the implementation to frontend-design, or explicitly defer to frontend-design — it should NOT silently become a code generator. May still read stacks/react.csv to inform the handoff.

assertions.text: does not silently turn into a full component-code generator in place of frontend-design
hands the implementation off to frontend-design (passing the brief / stack rules)

evals.name: accessibility-grounded-in-data
evals.prompt: Do an accessibility pass on a data-table-heavy admin screen — what are the must-fix items?
evals.expected_output: Should read data/accessibility/wcag-checklist.md (and aria-patterns.md / relevant ux-heuristics for tables) and return the P0 must-fix items grounded in that data, not generic invented advice. Should reference table-specific guidance where available.

assertions.text: reads the accessibility/ data (wcag-checklist / aria-patterns) rather than inventing generic a11y tips
surfaces prioritized (P0) must-fix items rather than an unordered grab-bag

evals.name: design-read-dials-and-anti-default-screen
evals.prompt: Make me a modern SaaS landing page design — make it pop, something that looks really premium and AI-first.
evals.expected_output: A vague 'make it pop / AI-first' prompt is exactly what tempts the LLM defaults. The brief must first state a one-line Design Read (screen / audience / vibe), set the three dials (DESIGN_VARIANCE / MOTION_INTENSITY / VISUAL_DENSITY) from that read, and actively screen against the universal anti-default clichés in references/anti-default.md — NOT reach for an AI-purple/indigo gradient on dark mesh, a centered hero, three equal cards, blanket glassmorphism, or Inter as the display face. If it deliberately keeps one of those, it must justify it as a choice, not a default. Tests that the skill reads the room and dodges the clichés instead of producing the default 'AI-first SaaS' look. Still routes through the data and ends with a frontend-design handoff.

assertions.text: states a one-line Design Read (screen / audience / vibe) before deciding
sets the three dials (variance / motion / density) explicitly in the brief
does not default to an AI-purple/indigo gradient, centered-hero-on-dark-mesh, or Inter display face; if any cliché is kept it is justified, not reached for by default
still hands implementation off to frontend-design rather than writing the page

evals.name: brand-never-guess
evals.prompt: Design direction for the Proxmox community dashboard we're building — it should feel on-brand with Proxmox.
evals.expected_output: A recognizable brand (Proxmox) is in scope and no brand-spec exists yet. The skill must follow references/brand-assets.md: it must NOT state Proxmox's brand hex from memory. With WebFetch available it pins the values from an official source (site CSS / svgl / simpleicons) and records source URL + fetch date, then writes docs/design/brand/proxmox-spec.md; without network it asks the user for the values. Style/type decisions still come from the vendored data; the brand-spec overrides on color only.

assertions.text: no brand hex value is asserted from memory — every brand color is either fetched (with source URL + date) or requested from the user
when values are obtained, a brand-spec file is written for reuse (docs/design/brand/<brand>-spec.md)
vendored data still picks the style; the brand-spec overrides color only
